candidates.title: Mac keyboard and trackpad sharing

demandEvidence.chore: I couldn't find a free keyboard/mouse sharing tool that handled the Apple trackpad well, so I set about directing the robots to make one.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: I couldn't find a free keyboard/mouse sharing tool that handled the Apple trackpad well, so I set about directing the robots to make one.

ease.reason: A narrow compatibility prototype is conceivable, but no supplied implementation source documents Mac input sharing or trackpad behavior.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: Mac users or support consultants might pay for setup help; this product-build post gives no payment evidence.

feasibility.reason: A four-week mock can document a test matrix, but real device sharing depends on low-level Mac behavior not established by the source.

autonomy.reason: The post describes building a tool, not an operating loop; a person must test devices and resolve input failures.

evidence.reason: The post directly identifies difficulty finding a free sharing tool with Apple trackpad support, but gives no repeat frequency or corroboration.

candidates.reason: Below threshold (4.0 mean). The request identifies a Mac keyboard/mouse sharing gap, but a small useful test depends on undocumented device-level behavior and lacks implementation references; payment is unproven.

candidates.title: Daily build metadata alert

demandEvidence.chore: The plan is to have a schedule trigger fetch the latest version metadata every morning, parse the JSON response, and send an alert to our Discord channel whenever a new build is detected.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: The plan is to have a schedule trigger fetch the latest version metadata every morning, parse the JSON response, and send an alert to our Discord channel whenever a new build is detected.

ease.reason: A beginner can prototype a scheduled fetch and parse using test metadata, though no supplied reference documents the integration.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: a small software consultancy might pay for this alert setup; the post establishes neither a buyer nor willingness to pay.

feasibility.reason: A four-week test can use one public metadata endpoint and a test Discord channel; endpoint and delivery failures need handling.

autonomy.reason: A scheduled check and alert are repeatable, while a person must validate the endpoint, alert content, and any response to a build.

evidence.reason: The post gives a concrete daily trigger, metadata parsing, and Discord alert, but no successful run, frequency of useful alerts, or implementation reference.

candidates.reason: Below threshold (5.4 mean). The post specifies a daily metadata-to-Discord alert, but no supplied building reference supports the integration and the post does not establish operational success or a paying customer.
